title: Competing symmetry breaking and topology in quantum spin chains
authors: Anthony Rey, Ömer M. Aksoy, Claudio Chamon, Akira Furusaki, Christopher Mudry
abstract: We investigate how spontaneous symmetry breaking and symmetry-protected topology compete and cooperate in one-dimensional quantum spin-1/2 systems. We introduce two families of local Hamiltonians with $\mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}^{T}_{2}$ symmetry which host a zoo of broken-symmetry phases with and without gapless boundary spins, namely, six long-range-ordered gapped phases that differ by their $\mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2}$-symmetry-breaking patterns (FM$^{\,}_{x,y,z}$ and Neel$^{\,}_{x,y,z}$), their partner symmetry-protected topological phases (FM$^{\mathrm{SPT}}_{x,y}$ and Neel$^{\mathrm{SPT}}_{x,y}$), and two gapless phases (gFM$^{\,}_{z}$ and gNeel$^{\,}_{z}$) with incommensurate $\mathbb{Z}^{T}_{2}$-breaking magnetic long-range order and central charge $\mathsf{c}=1$. Direct transitions between competing gapped phases can be continuous or weakly first order. We demonstrate that continuous phase transition lines have exotic critical properties. For example, a line of deconfined quantum critical points (between the Neel$^{\,}_{x}$ and Neel$^{\,}_{y}$ phases) described by Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid theory is terminated by the gFM$^{\,}_{z}$ phase at a Lifshitz tricritical point which exhibits spontaneous breaking of the continuous U(1) symmetry despite the locality and one-dimensionality of the Hamiltonian, contrary to a naive expectation from the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner-Coleman theorem. Furthermore, critical lines between symmetry-protected topological phases with different $\mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2}$-symmetry breaking (e.g., Neel$^{\mathrm{SPT}}_{x}$ and Neel$^{\mathrm{SPT}}_{y}$) additionally retain low-energy boundary degrees of freedom, realizing symmetry-enriched criticality (or a gapless SPT phase). Our results reveal unconventional mechanisms by which competing symmetry breaking and topology generate ordered critical phases and multicriticality.
summary: This work explores how competing symmetry breaking and topological order manifest in 1D quantum spin chains. By mapping out the phase diagram, the authors identify multiple ordered and gapless phases, revealing exotic critical behavior. The research highlights unconventional mechanisms where symmetry and topology cooperate to generate complex quantum critical points.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay between spontaneous symmetry breaking and symmetry-protected topology in one-dimensional quantum spin-1/2 systems.
main_result: The system exhibits a rich phase diagram featuring six distinct gapped phases, two gapless phases, and exotic critical points, including a Lifshitz tricritical point that breaks continuous symmetry unexpectedly.
method: The study combines theoretical analysis (e.g., Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid theory) with numerical techniques like DMRG and exact diagonalization to map out the phase diagram.
model_or_system: The model consists of one-dimensional quantum spin-1/2 lattice Hamiltonians possessing $\mathbb{Z}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ symmetry. The analysis is performed on the coupling space $T^2$.
key_observables: Symmetry-breaking patterns (FM, Neel), topological attributes (SPT phases), gap status, central charge ($c=1$), and ground-state degeneracy.
important_parameters: Coupling parameters $(\theta, \lambda)$ defining the Hamiltonian, and system size $2N$ for finite-size scaling analysis.
main_assumptions: The classification of SPT phases relies on the change in ground-state degeneracy with boundary conditions; the analysis involves approximations for sums and limits for large system sizes.
figures_summary: Figures 1, 2, and 3 depict the phase diagrams in the coupling space $T^2$ and along specific cuts, illustrating the various ordered, topological, and critical regions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by analyzing fixed points, constructing the phase diagram across the $T^2$ coupling space, and then performing detailed theoretical analyses of the critical lines and boundary physics.
why_interesting: The findings on symmetry-enriched criticality and the breakdown of naive symmetry theorems in 1D systems provide deep insights into how topology and symmetry constrain quantum ground states, relevant for understanding exotic phases in correlated materials.
